test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 06 Sept, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Two trains of equal length are running on parallel lines in the same direction at 36 km/h and 54 km/h. The faster train passes the slower train in 48 seconds. The length of each train (in m) is:
solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the first train = 36 km/h.

Speed of the second train = 54 km/h.

Both trains run in the same direction, and the faster the train passes the slower in 48 seconds.

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed = Difference in speed when two objects are moving in the same direction.

Distance = Speed × Time.

**Calculation:**

The relative speed of the two trains = (54 - 36) km/h = 18 km/h.

Converting speed into m/s by multiplying with,

⇒ Relative speed = 18 × (5)/(18) m/s = 5 m/s.

Time taken to pass = 48 seconds.

Using Distance = Speed × Time,

⇒ Distance = 5 m/s × 48 s = 240 m.

Since the distance covered is equal to the sum of the lengths of both trains and they are of equal length, let the length of each train be L.

⇒ 2L = 240 m.

⇒ L = 120 m.

**The length of each train is 120 m.**
